In [[algebraic topology]], the '''doomsday conjecture''' was a conjecture about [[Ext group]]s over the [[Steenrod algebra]] made by Joel Cohen, named by Michael Barratt, published by {{harvtxt|Milgram|1971|loc=conjecture 73}} and disproved by {{harvtxt|Mahowald|1977}}. {{harvtxt|Minami|1995}} stated a modified version called the '''new doomsday conjecture'''.

The original doomsday conjecture was that for any prime ''p'' and positive integer ''s'' there are only a finite number of permanent cycles in

:<math>\text{Ext}_{A_*}^{s,*}(Z/pZ,Z/pZ). \,</math>

{{harvtxt|Mahowald|1977}} found an infinite number of permanent cycles for ''p''&nbsp;=&nbsp;''s''&nbsp;=&nbsp;2, disproving the conjecture.  Minami's new doomsday conjecture is a weaker form stating (in the case ''p''&nbsp;=&nbsp;2) that there are no nontrivial permanent cycles in the image of (Sq<sup>0</sup>)<sup>''n''</sup> for ''n'' sufficiently large depending on&nbsp;''s''.
